repos.audit_reason: The oracle stops at its first real step: curl -f gets HTTP 403 AccessDenied for the BERT-Tiny zip. That is the exact checkpoint URL listed in the README (line 48), and other official bert_models URLs also return 403. The installing agent's /work/setup.sh also notes the official GCS zip is gone. The README's documented model download is dead upstream, so the documented demo cannot be reproduced as written. This is not an oracle bug.
repos.public_reason: Every pretrained BERT checkpoint the README links (storage.googleapis.com/bert_models/...) now returns HTTP 403 Access Denied, so the feature-extraction demo has no model to load.

attribution_evidence: README mentions 'Google Brain' -> team Google Research (low)
repos.audit_reason: The README snippet (README.md:68-85) loads its pre-trained weights and vocab from gs://trax-ml, and that bucket now gives anonymous callers a 403 (AccessDenied), so the documented demo cannot run anywhere. The sandbox's GCS access works fine: a known public bucket returns 206. The oracle copies the README snippet faithfully, so the fault is in the repo's documented resources, not in the oracle.
repos.public_reason: The README's pre-trained translation weights and vocabulary live in the gs://trax-ml bucket, which now returns HTTP 403 Access Denied to everyone, and the repo is archived.

repos.audit_reason: The oracle stopped at `test -d checkpoints/coco_pretrained` because checkpoints/ is empty. The pretrained-model tarball that README.md line 65 points to on Google Drive (id 12gvlTbMvUcJewQlSEaZdeb2CdOB-b8kQ) now returns HTTP 404, and gdown can't fetch it either, so the README's documented COCO test demo can't be run. The oracle's check is reasonable; the repo's required download is broken.
repos.public_reason: The README's Google Drive link to the pretrained checkpoints returns 404 (reported in issue #175), so the pretrained-model demo cannot run.
